clue.text: What one must do to succeed in business

definitions.text: What one must do to succeed in business

parts.words: What one must do to succeed in business
parts.note: the whole clue describes the basic goal of any trader: earning more than is spent

explanation.definitionFit: Success in commerce is measured by ending up with gains over costs.

clue.text: Full-size rug with rude sort of finish

parts.note: a mat is a small rug

indicators.note: a sort of the word rude is a rearranged version of its letters

explanation.surface: Describing a large rug with a crude kind of edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full-size' reads as describing the rug, but it is the definition, meaning grown up; 'sort of' is the anagram signal and the shuffled word comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fully grown or developed has reached its adult size.

clue.text: Tyne barges, perhaps, or what they are built on

definitions.meaning: flat-bottomed coal boats on the River Tyne in north-east England were called by this name
the backbone timber along the bottom of a ship's hull

explanation.surface: A question about boats on a northern English river and their construction.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Tyneside coal boat and the structural spine of any hull.

clue.text: Take the innkeeper's part?

parts.note: reads like casting a stage role, but means doing what a landlord does: welcoming guests

explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper entertains and receives visitors, which is the role of one who welcomes people in.

clue.text: Kind of knot sailors will be well advised to avoid

definitions.meaning: a square knot tied with two crossed overhand turns

definitions.text: sailors will be well advised to avoid
definitions.meaning: a ridge of rock or coral just below the sea surface, a shipping hazard

explanation.surface: A knot that seamen ought to steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a square knot used in sail-shortening and a hazardous submerged ridge.

clue.text: Readiness to accept whatever life has to offer

definitions.text: Readiness to accept whatever life has to offer

parts.words: Readiness to accept whatever life has to offer
parts.note: describes the outlook that events are predetermined and must simply be accepted

explanation.definitionFit: The belief that all events are fixed by destiny leads to resigned acceptance.

clue.text: What Seneca was to Nero in his formative years

definitions.text: What Seneca was to Nero in his formative years

parts.words: What Seneca was to Nero in his formative years
parts.note: the Stoic philosopher Seneca taught the young future emperor Nero

explanation.definitionFit: Seneca acted as private teacher to the boy Nero.

clue.text: Loose-fitting coat for an anaemic toddler

parts.note: an anaemic person looks pale
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Advice on outerwear for a sickly-looking small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose overcoat, a French borrowing.

clue.text: Part-time journalist required to mend a tennis racket, possibly?

definitions.meaning: a freelance local correspondent paid by the piece

definitions.text: required to mend a tennis racket, possibly?
definitions.meaning: a person who fits new strings to rackets

explanation.surface: A freelance reporter needed to repair sports equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a casual newspaper correspondent and someone who restrings rackets.

clue.text: Means of remedying behaviour to others?

definitions.meaning: medical care given to cure an illness
the way one deals with or handles people

explanation.surface: A cure for how someone acts toward other people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both medical care and the manner of dealing with people.

clue.text: Unqualified lot

definitions.meaning: complete, absolute, as in an utter disaster
the whole amount, the sum

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both utter or complete and the whole sum.

clue.text: Is among those left to carry on the fight

indicators.note: the word Is goes among the letters of the remainder, placed within it

parts.note: the rest are the remaining ones
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone among the survivors who keeps on fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is among those left' reads as a whole phrase, but 'among' is the container signal; the definition is the final 'carry on the fight'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep fighting is to hold out against an opponent.

clue.text: Scaremongering little Roman god penetrating a thin fog

indicators.note: the god's name pierces into the phrase a thin fog, going between its parts

parts.note: a mist is a light fog
a lar was one of the minor Roman household gods, the lares

explanation.surface: A minor deity alarmingly entering a misty scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The lares were small guardian spirits of the Roman home, hence 'little'; 'penetrating' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: One who spreads needless fear is a scaremonger, which works as an adjective here too.

clue.text: I hold every man a to his profession" (Bacon)

definitions.text: I hold every man a to his profession" (Bacon)

parts.words: I hold every man a to his profession" (Bacon)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Francis Bacon's preface to his Maxims of the Law; the missing word means one who owes

explanation.walkthrough: The gap falls after 'a': Bacon's line is that every man owes something to his profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon's word for a man who owes a duty is one in debt.

clue.text: Massachusetts art gallery crowned with laurels, apparently

indicators.note: in a down entry the gallery has the laurels placed on top of it, coming first

parts.note: bays are laurel leaves, as worn in victory wreaths
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: An American state likened to a gallery wearing a victor's wreath.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's national gallery of British and modern art. 'crowned with' puts BAYS above TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Massachusetts' official nickname is the Bay State, after Massachusetts Bay.

clue.text: Cart goes another way to get a French table delicacy

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are arranged in a different way

explanation.surface: A cart taking a different road to fetch a fancy French dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails cooked in garlic butter are a classic dish of French cuisine.

clue.text: In vain he strove to get the gold from St Michael's

definitions.text: In vain he strove to get the gold

indicators.note: the answer is made out of the letters of the saint's name, rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A man who toiled fruitlessly for treasure from a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to build the answer out of ST MICHAEL; the possessive 's gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval experimenters tried in vain to turn base metal into gold.

clue.text: At a discount? Well, not altogether

definitions.meaning: below face value, as stock sold cheaply
slightly unwell, not quite healthy

explanation.surface: A question about a bargain answered with a hesitant reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both priced below nominal value and feeling a little ill.

clue.text: Attempt to overcharge someone for fixingalovers'meeting?

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to sting is slang for cheating someone out of money

explanation.surface: Trying to fleece a couple who are arranging a romantic rendezvous.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue runs 'fixing a lovers' meeting' together; it is the definition. A tryst is a secret meeting of lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging a secret romantic rendezvous is making a tryst.

clue.text: Far from interesting outside broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of outside are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An outside broadcast described as dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside broadcast' looks like a TV term, but 'broadcast' scatters the letters of OUTSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and boring is the opposite of interesting.

clue.text: Afraid to show concern about things in South Dakota

indicators.note: the worry is set within the state's abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for the US state of South Dakota
care is concern or worry

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of showing anxiety while in South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: SD is the US postal code; 'in' is the container signal, and 'to show' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frightened is a synonym of being afraid.

clue.text: Exhausted by his efforts, the artist dined out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter worn out by his work goes out for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Having one's energy used up through effort means being worn out.

clue.text: Exhaustive description of what the three blind mice were?

definitions.meaning: thorough, covering everything

definitions.text: description of what the three blind mice were?
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the mice's tails

explanation.surface: A thorough account of the nursery-rhyme mice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means thorough and, split as de-tailed, having had tails removed.

clue.text: Clubs that place cruel restrictions on members?

definitions.meaning: golf clubs with metal heads

definitions.text: that place cruel restrictions on members?
definitions.meaning: shackles or fetters on the limbs, members meaning arms and legs

explanation.surface: Societies that impose harsh rules on their membership.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both metal-headed golf clubs and chains for the limbs.

clue.text: Thanks to the French a Norman force ultimately took it over

definitions.text: Norman force ultimately took it over

parts.note: merci is French for thank you

explanation.surface: Gratitude in French for a Norman army that eventually conquered something.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of central England, absorbed after the Norman Conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon midland kingdom was eventually ruled by the Norman invaders.

clue.text: Small child in a big country

parts.note: CH is a standard abbreviation for child
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little child in a vast land.
explanation.definitionFit: China is one of the world's largest nations.

clue.text: Second-class letter

definitions.meaning: a ... grade marks second-rate work
the second character of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Post sent at the cheaper rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's second character also denotes a second-class grade.

clue.text: Surpass all others as a swindler?

definitions.meaning: beat or excel everyone
to do someone is to cheat them, so a swindler is out to do people

explanation.surface: Beating everyone, like a conman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to excel, and read as out-to-do describes a cheat's aim.

clue.text: Prices in a tangle? He will insist on getting them right

definitions.text: He will insist on getting them right

indicators.note: a tangle mixes things up, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Muddled prices fixed by a stickler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a tangle' looks like the indicator, but 'in a' is fodder with PRICES and 'tangle' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A precisian is a pedant strict about exact correctness.

clue.text: Helpful girl who may have to wait for her pay

definitions.text: Helpful girl who may have to wait for her pay

parts.words: Helpful girl who may have to wait for her pay
parts.note: wait means wait at table, the domestic duty of a female household help

explanation.definitionFit: A female domestic servant waits on her employers.
